title: Install, test and maintain a basic hydraulic system

lessons.title: How hydraulic systems work
lessons.html:
Hydraulics on farm equipment

Hydraulics use oil under pressure to transmit power. On tractors, hydraulics lift the three-point linkage, steer the front wheels, operate front-end loaders and tip trailers. Implements such as balers, planters, sprayers and harrows use hydraulic cylinders and motors to fold, lift and drive parts.

The basic principle

Liquids hardly compress. When a force pushes on oil in a closed system, the pressure spreads equally in all directions (Pascal's principle). Pressure = force ÷ area. A small force on a small piston can produce a large force on a large piston. This is why a hydraulic cylinder can lift a heavy implement.

Main components

ComponentFunction
Reservoir (tank)Stores oil, allows air to separate and helps cool the oil
FilterRemoves dirt from the oil; suction, pressure or return filters
PumpCreates flow (gear, vane or piston type). The pump creates flow; pressure builds when that flow meets resistance
Relief valveLimits maximum pressure to protect the system
Directional control valveDirects oil to and from actuators (for example lift, neutral, lower)
Flow control valveControls the speed of actuators
ActuatorsCylinders give straight-line motion; motors give rotary motion
Hoses, pipes and fittingsCarry oil between components
AccumulatorStores oil under pressure; found on some systems

Open-centre and closed-centre

In an open-centre system, oil flows back to the tank when the valve is in neutral. In a closed-centre system, the valve blocks flow in neutral and the pump adjusts its output. Many modern tractors use load-sensing closed-centre systems. Always check the manual for the system type.

Reading circuit diagrams

Hydraulic circuits are drawn with standard symbols: a circle with a triangle for a pump, a rectangle with a rod for a cylinder, boxes with arrows for valves. Learning these symbols helps you trace faults and install components correctly.

lessons.title: Safety and installing components
lessons.html:
Hydraulic safety

Hydraulic systems store a lot of energy and can cause serious injuries.

  • Fluid injection: oil escaping from a pinhole leak at high pressure can penetrate skin. It may look like a small wound but can cause severe tissue damage. Get medical help immediately; it is a medical emergency.
  • Never feel for leaks with your hand. Use a piece of cardboard or wood.
  • Falling loads: lower implements to the ground or support them with stands before working under them. Never rely on hydraulics alone to hold a load.
  • Stored pressure: release pressure before disconnecting hoses. Switch off the engine and move control levers back and forth as the manual says. Accumulators may hold pressure even when the engine is off.
  • Hot oil: can burn. Let the system cool.
  • Wear safety glasses and gloves.

Installing components

  1. Get the correct part: check part numbers, pressure ratings, thread types and sizes against the manual.
  2. Lower or support all loads and release pressure.
  3. Clean around fittings before opening so dirt does not enter.
  4. Cap or plug open ports and hose ends immediately.
  5. Fit new O-rings and seals of the correct type; lightly lubricate with clean hydraulic oil.
  6. Tighten fittings to the specified torque. Do not over-tighten, which can damage threads and flare seats.
  7. Route hoses without twists, sharp bends or rubbing on edges. Allow for movement of the implement. Use clamps and protective sleeves where needed.
  8. Use hoses of the correct pressure rating and length.

Cleanliness

Dirt is the main enemy of hydraulic systems. A tiny particle can score a valve spool or pump. Keep containers, funnels and work areas clean, and use only the oil type and grade specified by the manufacturer. Mixing incompatible oils can damage seals.

Quick couplers

Clean couplers before connecting implements. Check for leaks and damage. Replace dust caps after disconnecting.

lessons.title: Testing, fault-finding and maintenance
lessons.html:
Testing after installation

  1. Check the oil level and top up with the correct oil.
  2. Start the engine at low idle with all controls in neutral.
  3. Operate each function slowly through its full stroke several times to bleed air from the system.
  4. Check for leaks at all joints using cardboard, not your hand.
  5. Check the oil level again after cycling and top up.
  6. Test operating speed and smoothness.
  7. Where required and trained, connect a pressure gauge to the test point and compare readings, such as relief valve pressure, with the manual's specification.
  8. Record results on the job card.

Common faults and causes

SymptomPossible causes
Slow or weak operationLow oil level, blocked filter, worn pump, internal leakage, relief valve set too low
Noisy pumpAir in oil, low oil level, blocked suction filter, cavitation
OverheatingLow oil, wrong oil, relief valve blowing constantly, blocked cooler
Foaming oilAir leak on suction side, wrong oil, low level
Cylinder creeps downWorn piston seals, leaking control valve
External leaksDamaged hoses, loose fittings, worn seals

Work methodically: start with simple checks such as oil level and filters before suspecting major components.

Preventive maintenance

  • Check oil level daily or as the manual says.
  • Change filters and oil at the specified intervals.
  • Inspect hoses for cracks, bulges, abrasion and leaks; replace damaged hoses.
  • Keep cylinder rods clean and check for scoring or bends.
  • Grease pivot points.
  • Keep couplers and breathers clean.
  • Take an oil sample for analysis if your operation does this.

Environmental care

Catch oil in drip trays. Clean spills with absorbent. Dispose of used oil and filters through an approved recycler. Never pour oil onto the ground.

Key points

  • The pump creates flow; pressure builds against resistance.
  • Never feel for leaks with your hand; oil injection is a medical emergency.
  • Support loads and release pressure before working on the system.
  • Keep everything clean and use the specified oil.
  • Bleed air, check leaks and test pressures after installation.
  • Start fault-finding with simple checks like oil level and filters.
